cap: Timing decides the injury. In the first 2 weeks exposure is all or none, organogenesis in weeks 3 to 8 produces major malformations organ by organ, and the fetal period causes growth and functional injury. The brain stays vulnerable throughout, while kidneys, teeth, ears and the ductus arteriosus are hurt late.
teach: Weeks here count from fertilization, so gestational age is 2 weeks more. The neural tube closes by about day 28 after conception, before many patients know they are pregnant, which is why folic acid starts before conception. Valproate and carbamazepine act on the neural tube, thalidomide and methotrexate on the limbs, lithium and isotretinoin on the heart, and isotretinoin and mycophenolate on the face and ears. ACE inhibitors and ARBs injure the fetal kidney after the first trimester, tetracyclines stain developing teeth, aminoglycosides injure the eighth nerve, and NSAIDs close the ductus arteriosus late in pregnancy. Alcohol injures the brain at any stage. Radiation harms the fetal brain only at high doses; no harm is shown below 50 mGy. Drugs cross the placenta by diffusion when they are small, lipid soluble and un-ionized, so heparin, which is large and charged, does not reach the fetus.
